refactor: clean up auto-align code (#810)

* chore: update snapshots for pandas/polars dtype changes

Pandas 2.x uses "str" dtype for string columns instead of "object",
and polars list columns now get "center" alignment. These snapshot
updates reflect the current behavior with the existing codebase.

* Revert "chore: update snapshots for pandas/polars dtype changes"

This reverts commit 7764660cb652442dca54c9559a616286c6b4add0.

* fix: support pandas 3.x "str" dtype in auto-alignment

Pandas 3.x uses "str" dtype for string columns instead of "object".
This change:
- Adds "str" to the set of dtypes that get left-aligned
- Extends number-like detection to also check "str" dtype columns,
  so string columns with numeric-looking values still get right-aligned

This maintains consistent behavior across pandas 2.x and 3.x.

* refactor: extract auto-alignment logic to _tbl_data_align module

Extract dtype classification logic from Boxhead.align_from_data() into
a dedicated module using singledispatch for cleaner separation of concerns.

Changes:
- Create _tbl_data_align.py with classify_dtype_for_alignment() and
  is_number_like_column() functions
- Simplify align_from_data() to use the new module
- Add comprehensive tests in test_tbl_data_align.py (32 tests)

The refactor preserves existing behavior:
- Uses re.match (not re.search) to match original _str_detect behavior
- Supports both pandas 2.x ("object") and 3.x ("str") string dtypes
- Number-like string detection works for both dtype variants

* test: add PyArrow tests for dtype classification

Add tests for PyArrow backend coverage in test_tbl_data_align.py:
- TestClassifyDtypePyArrow class with numeric, string, bool, date tests
- PyArrow number-like detection tests
- PyArrow integration tests with GT

Coverage for _tbl_data_align.py increased from 74% to 87%.

fix: cols_*() methods silently ignore invalid column names in a list

cols_align, cols_label_with, cols_hide, cols_unhide, cols_move,
cols_move_to_start, cols_move_to_end, and cols_reorder raise when a
single invalid column name is passed as a string, but silently drop
invalid names when passed inside a list, since resolve_cols_c() drops
unmatched names before any validation runs.

Validate the originally requested column names directly instead of
relying on the already-filtered resolved list.

table unchanged instead, matching R's gt and other selection based methods.

Closes #714

fix(nanoplots): warn when a curved data line is dropped for x_vals

A curved data line is interpolated from evenly spaced x positions, so
supplying x_vals silently reset data_line_type to 'straight' halfway through
the function. Move that fallback to a guard at the top and warn, so the
override is visible to users and easy to spot in the code.

fix(formats): pad the year in the iso date style

The iso style is defined as 'y-MM-dd', and in CLDR 'y' is the year with no
minimum width, so a year below 1000 loses its leading zeros: 0999-01-05 comes
out as 999-01-05, which great_tables' own _iso_str_to_date and
datetime.date.fromisoformat both reject.

Use 'yyyy-MM-dd' so the style produces a valid ISO 8601 date. Four-digit years
are unaffected.

fix(latex): emit one cell per column in a spanner row

A group of columns with no spanner was written as a single cell, because
'"" * span' is always the empty string, and span_accumulator only grew inside
the spanner branch. A spanner row therefore carried fewer cells than the table
has columns, and the cmidrule under a spanner pointed at columns to the left of
the ones it covers.

With a 5 column table and a spanner over the third and fourth, the row held 4
cells and the rule read 2-3 instead of 3-4. Short rows are what makes the first
column stretch under extracolsep.

Emit one cell per covered column and count every group, spanned or not, when
resolving the cmidrule bounds.

fix(latex): escape backslash, tilde and circumflex with their macros

_latex_escape prefixed a backslash to every special character, which is
correct for & % $ # _ { } but wrong for the remaining three: a doubled
backslash is a line break, and a prefixed tilde or circumflex is an accent
that takes the next character as its argument. A cell holding a Windows path
either shifted the row or failed to compile.

The R gt package maps these three to \textbackslash{}, \textasciitilde{} and
\textasciicircum{}, which its decode_latex_special_chars reverses.

fix(utils): match options on a prefix instead of a substring

_match_arg accepted any option containing the supplied value anywhere, and
resolved ties with matched.pop(), so a typo was silently accepted as whatever
option happened to come last: opt_align_table_header(align="ight") returned
"right", align="e" returned "center", and align="" matched every option.

Options may still be abbreviated, now by a prefix, which is what match.arg in
R does. An exact match wins over a prefix shared with longer options, and an
ambiguous abbreviation raises instead of picking one.

fix(formats): accept locale names regardless of case

Locale handling replaced underscores with hyphens and then compared the result
against the known locales as an exact string, so the case of a BCP 47 tag
decided whether it was accepted: locale="pt-BR" formatted, locale="pt-br"
raised ValueError. The error even called the value "the normalized locale
name", although the case was never normalized.

Case in a BCP 47 tag is a writing convention, not meaning, so the lookup now
matches without regard to case and resolves to the spelling the locale data
uses. Unknown locales still raise.

fix(utils): match the http scheme case-insensitively

URI schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 3986, Section 3.1), but
is_valid_http_schema() compared the prefix verbatim, so a value like
HTTPS://example.com/logo.png was not recognized as remote.

In fmt_image() that value falls through to the local-file branch, where
Path() collapses the double slash and the image is read from disk:

    FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
    '/current/dir/HTTPS:/example.com/logo.png'

With encode=False the failure is silent instead: the src attribute gets
a local path built from the remote URL.

test(helpers): stop the parametrized _intify_scaled_px test from being shadowed

tests/test_helpers.py defines test_intify_scaled_px twice: a parametrized
version at line 408 and a plain one at line 488. The second definition
rebinds the name, so pytest only ever collects the later one and the
three parametrized cases never run.

    pytest tests/test_helpers.py -k intify --collect-only
    before: 1 test
    after:  5 tests

The cases are merged into the parametrized test, and the truncating
behavior that 5px * 1.5 == 7 documents is now spelled out in a comment
so it is not mistaken for a rounding bug later.

fix(options): keep the fractional part when scaling padding

opt_vertical_padding() and opt_horizontal_padding() ran the scaled value
through int(), so a fraction was truncated and a small scale collapsed
the padding to 0px:

    heading_padding is 4px
    opt_vertical_padding(scale=0.1) -> 0px, where R gt emits 0.4px

CSS accepts sub-pixel lengths, and R gt keeps the fraction: it multiplies
and re-attaches the unit in get_padding_option_value_list(). The TODO on
both call sites described the integer result as a limitation rather than
a decision, so both are now gone.

_intify_scaled_px() is replaced by _scaled_px(), which returns an int
when the result lands on a whole number, so 8px scaled by 1.5 still
renders as '12px' and not '12.0px', the same as R.

The result is rounded to four decimal places, which is not cosmetic:
5px scaled by 0.07 is 0.35000000000000003 in binary floating point, and
that would otherwise be written into the stylesheet. 263 of 1800
scale/value combinations in the accepted range produce an artifact like
that.

fix(render): render booleans, missing values and zero the same on every backend

cast_frame_to_string() let each backend decide how a value becomes text,
so the same logical table read differently depending on the dataframe
library it was built from:

    value    pandas   polars   pyarrow
    True     True     true     true
    missing  <NA>     None     None
    -0.0     -0.0     -0.0     -0

Per the decision in #875: booleans render as True/False, missing values
as None, and zero carries no sign.

- Booleans are normalized in the polars and pyarrow branches. Only
  boolean columns are touched, so a string column that happens to spell
  'true' is left alone.
- Floating point columns get a zero added before the cast, which turns
  -0.0 into 0.0 and leaves every other value untouched. In polars an
  explicit when/then is needed, because adding zero is optimized away.
- pandas emits pd.NA, which renders as '<NA>'. Converting it to None
  also required replace_null_frame(), since under the 'string' dtype a
  None coming from the replacement is coerced straight back to pd.NA.

Not addressed here, because #875 did not settle it: pyarrow still writes
a whole float as '0' where pandas and polars write '0.0'. That is float
formatting rather than a spelling difference, and fmt_number() is the
place to decide it.
Preserve integer CSS values in css_add()

fix(nanoplots): drop the positions whose x value is missing

The mask that decides which positions survive was built with `~_is_na(val)`.
On a bool, `~` is a bitwise inversion, not a negation: it yields -2 for True
and -1 for False, and both are truthy. Every position was therefore kept, the
missing x value reached `_normalize_to_dict()`, came back as None, and the
plot died on `data_x_width * None`.

Python agrees this is a trap: 3.14 warns that this "is usually not what you
expect from negating a bool" and 3.16 removes the operation on bools.

The test that covered this was marked xfail with the bug written down; it now
passes and the marker is gone. A second test pins the guarantee the comment
above the mask makes and nothing checked: dropping an x position drops the y
value paired with it, so the plot matches the one built from the surviving
pairs.
